mainTopic: רב פפא's version of the contradiction between the purse case in our משנה and the wine-from-כותים case in מסכת דמאי, the answer, and the closing הדרן of מסכת מעילה
overview: This amud gives one more version of ריש לקיש's question about the purse case in our משנה. רב פפא sets that case against a משנה in דמאי about wine bought from כותים. In that משנה, רבי מאיר lets the buyer say that portions of wine he will separate in the future are תרומה and מעשרות, and then drink right away. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid this, because at the time he speaks nobody knows which wine those portions are. The purse ruling seems to rely on that same idea, since only the last coin left turns out to be the holy one. The answer is that the end of our משנה is about someone who said 'this purse will not be free of הקדש,' so his own words make the last coin the holy one. The amud then closes the פרק השליח שעשה שליחותו and all of מסכת מעילה with the הדרן.

steps.title: רב פפא sets the purse case against the wine case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives his version of the question: our משנה about purses contradicts a משנה about לוגין of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He raised a contradiction between the purses and the לוגין, as we learned in a משנה: One who buys wine from among the כותים...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another version of the question asked earlier. He says the contradiction was between the purse case in our משנה and a משנה about measures of wine, and he starts quoting that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is setup. It names the two sources being compared and opens the quote of the second one. The details that make the contradiction sharp come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Purses, meaning the purse-of-coins case in our משנה
He 'threw' one source against another, meaning he raised a contradiction
כותים (Samaritans), who were suspected of not separating תרומה and מעשרות

phrases.english: He raised a contradiction between purses and log measures,
phrases.notes: 'Purses' is the purse-of-coins case in our משנה, and 'log measures' is the wine case he's about to quote.

phrases.english: as we learned: One who buys wine from among the Kutim

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of ריש לקיש's question, which was discussed before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the end of our משנה about the purse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The purse ruling treats the last coin left as the holy one, as if it had been holy all along, even though nobody knew which coin it was when he spent the others. In the wine משנה, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון reject this kind of later identification. Even רבי מאיר allows it only when the person says outright 'that I will separate in the future.' In the purse case, any coin he spends might be the holy one.

steps.title: The wine case: רבי מאיר permits, three תנאים forbid
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר lets the buyer name the תרומה and מעשרות he will separate in the future and drink now. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: 'Two לוגין that I will separate in the future are תרומה, ten are מעשר ראשון, nine are מעשר שני.' He redeems the מעשר שני and drinks right away. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from דמאי. רבי מאיר lets the buyer name the portions of wine he will separate later and drink now, but three other תנאים forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's method only works if we say that the wine separated later was the תרומה and מעשר all along. The three other תנאים do not accept this, because at the time he speaks nobody knows which wine those portions are. Our משנה's purse ruling seems to rely on this same idea, since only the last coin left turns out to be the holy one, and it lacks even רבי מאיר's explicit 'that I will separate' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to the כהן
First tithe, given to the לוי
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed with money
Redeems, moving the holiness of the מעשר שני onto money

steps.confusionAlert: The numbers come from a barrel of 100 לוגין: 2 (one-fiftieth) for תרומה, 10 for מעשר ראשון, and 9 (one-tenth of the remaining 90) for מעשר שני. The numbers are just an example. The real issue is whether you can drink now and separate later.

phrases.english: he says: 'Two log that I will separate in the future
and he redeems it and drinks immediately,
phrases.notes: He redeems the מעשר שני he'll separate later onto money, so the wine can be drunk now.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the משנה that רב פפא sets against our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: you may name תרומה and מעשרות that will be separated later and drink now. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.

steps.title: The purse case is where he said the purse won't be free of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the end of our משנה is about someone who said 'this purse will not be exempt from הקדש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The end of our משנה is a case where the person said, 'This purse will not be exempt from הקדש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to the question is given. The end of our משנה is about a specific wording: 'this purse will not be free of הקדש.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With that wording, the person clearly means that whatever coin is left last is the holy one. So the case is no longer about an unknown portion to be picked out later, which is what made the wine case problematic. The contradiction goes away because the two cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: The end (latter clause) of a משנה
Will not be exempt / will not go free
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The purse case does not depend on naming something that will be picked out later. The person's words make the last coin left in the purse the holy one.

phrases.notes: This is the answer to the question; the earlier versions give it in רבי יוחנן's name.

phrases.english: The latter clause of our mishna

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹמֵר ״לֹא יִפָּטֵר כִּיס זֶה מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ״.
phrases.english: is where he says, 'This purse will not be exempt from consecration.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The purse case seemed to rely on a portion identified later, which the wine case treats as a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of our משנה is about someone who said the purse will not be free of הקדש, so the last coin left is the holy one.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing השליח שעשה שליחותו and מסכת מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק השליח שעשה שליחותו and for all of מסכת מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, השליח שעשה שליחותו, and מסכת מעילה is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the formula said when finishing a פרק. Here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no new argument here. It closes the last פרק and declares that the מסכת is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the formula for finishing a פרק
Misusing הקדש property for personal benefit

phrases.english: the agent who carried out his mission,
phrases.notes: That is the name of this פרק, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final answer.
